You are helping with an AUTHORIZED, READ-ONLY security audit of a Next.js App Router codebase at /opt/nxeon. These files are `"use server"` action modules — every exported async function is a remotely-invokable HTTP endpoint an attacker can POST to directly with arbitrary arguments. DO NOT EDIT ANYTHING. Only Read/grep.

Auth model (from /opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts): `requireUser()` returns the current user or throws; `requireAdmin()` throws unless ADMIN; `requireStaff()` staff-only. An action is IDOR-vulnerable if it accepts an id/serverId/volumeId/etc. as a parameter and acts on that object WITHOUT verifying the caller owns it (e.g. `db.server.findFirst({where:{id, userId: user.id}})` or a helper like `ownedServer()` that checks `server.userId !== user.id && user.role !== "ADMIN"`). A local helper that loads the object scoped to the user counts as a proper ownership check.

For EACH of these files:
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-ops.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-extra.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-nxcloud.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-disk.ts
/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts

Enumerate every EXPORTED async function that reaches a dangerous sink: `db.job.create` (enqueues a job the ROOT worker executes), `spawn`/`exec`/`execSync`, `writeFile`/SFTP write, credential/password mint or reset, or wallet/billing mutation. For each such function report EXACTLY:
- file:line and function name
- the auth guard present (quote the actual line, e.g. `await requireUser()` or `ownedServer(serverId)`), or NONE
- whether it verifies the caller OWNS the id argument before the sink (quote the ownership-check line, or write "NO OWNERSHIP CHECK")
- the job type / sink reached
- VERDICT: OK, or IDOR (owns-check missing), or NO-AUTH (no guard at all), or WEAK (e.g. requireUser where the capability is clearly admin-only infra)

Be precise and quote real lines with line numbers. Pay special attention to any function where a caller-supplied serverId flows into db.job.create without an ownership check, and to any job.payload that carries attacker-controlled structured data (not just {serverId} or {someId}). List those payload shapes. Keep it a tight bulleted list per file, most dangerous first. Do not speculate beyond what the code shows.
